name: Analyzing the Gap Between Chess Opening Theory and Practical Execution
description: A data curation and analysis project that investigates the relationship between chess opening theory and practical performance across player skill levels. Using the Lichess Open Database and the Encyclopedia of Chess Openings (ECO), this project builds an automated pipeline to download, clean, integrate, and analyze millions of rated online chess games. Win rates are computed per opening per rating group (beginner through master), cross-group variance is measured to identify theory-vs-practice gaps, and post-opening accuracy (Average Centipawn Loss) is correlated with ECO theoretical line length.

hasPart.name: Cleaned Games CSV

hasPart.name: Integrated Games CSV
hasPart.description: Cleaned games enriched with ECO opening classifications, theoretical line lengths, average Elo, and rating group assignments.

hasPart.name: ECO Opening Database Cache
hasPart.description: 3,690 named chess opening variations from the official lichess-org/chess-openings repository, with normalised move strings and computed line lengths.

hasPart.name: Analysis Results
hasPart.description: Per-opening win rate summaries, cross-group variance measurements, master vs beginner comparisons, and ACPL-by-line-length aggregations.
